title: Jules Verne's birth chart
metaDescription: Jules Verne's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.8° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the ten placements whose signs are settled, fixed leads with four. The fixed signs are the scheme’s ballast — mid-season, fully committed, expensive to turn.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 18.8° Aquarius, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mercury. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 22.7° Aquarius; Venus stands at 18.3° Pisces; Mars stands at 0.5° Sagittarius. The tradition reads thought that travels by comparison from Mercury, attraction that works by atmosphere from Venus, effort spent in bursts and openings from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Jupiter and Saturn — a trine holding at 0.7°. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, Mars sextile Uranus at 1.1°, and Venus sextile Neptune at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Venus, Jupiter, Saturn close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 18.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Scorpio at 14.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 18.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Cancer at 14.4° is in detriment. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements water 4, air 2, fire 2, earth 2; modalities fixed 4, cardinal 4, mutable 2. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. Saturn was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.4° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 14.4°.
